Cap.description: Which per-run cap ended a session.

oneOf.description: The cap on conversation turns.
The cap on cost.
The cap on wall-clock time.

Denial.description: A refusal of a tool call: who refused it and, when it says, why.

oneOf.description: The harness refused the call by its own rules.
A hook refused the call.
The user refused the call.

Digest.description: A content digest: `sha256:` followed by 64 lowercase hex digits.

EndedBy.description: How a session ended: an object whose `kind` is `completed`, `agent_error`, `cap`, `gateway_error`, `budget_stop`, `killed`, `interrupted` or `unknown`.

oneOf.description: The agent finished its work.
The agent reported an error, optionally with a reason code under `reason`.

reason.description: Why the agent failed, when it says.

oneOf.description: A per-run cap stopped the session; the key `cap` names it.
The gateway or the provider failed.
The job budget stopped the session.
The session was killed.
The supervisor was lost while the session ran.
The trace does not say how the session ended.

Event.description: One event of a session: its place in the session, what happened, the frame it came from, and the keys of the line that no field holds.

at.description: When the event happened, if the harness or the frame time says.

ext.description: Data of the harness that no other field holds: an open JSON object, empty when there is none, whose content is open, so a `null` inside it is kept and written back.

raw_ref.description: The frame the event was read from.

seq.$comment: Fits in 64 bits; the Rust reader enforces it.
seq.description: The position of the event in its session, counting from 0 without gaps.

span.description: The harness's id that pairs a call with its result, if the event has one.

EventKind.description: What happened at one point of a session: an object whose `kind` is `user_message`, `assistant_message`, `tool_call`, `tool_result`, `notification` or `usage`, with the members of that kind beside it.

oneOf.description: The user said something.

text.description: The text, if the harness records it.

oneOf.description: The assistant said something.

text.description: The text, if the harness records it.

oneOf.description: The assistant called a tool.

argv.description: The command line, if the tool runs one.

origin.description: Where the tool is served from.

wrapped_calls.description: The MCP calls this call bundles; an empty array when it bundles none.

oneOf.description: A tool call came back.

denied.description: Who refused the call, when it was refused.

is_error.description: Whether the result is an error.

oneOf.description: A line of the stream that is none of the other kinds; its content is in the event's `ext`.
Token counts and cost; a `session_total` is the running total of the session, so a later one supersedes an earlier one.

cache_creation_tokens.$comment: Fits in 64 bits; the Rust reader enforces it.
cache_creation_tokens.description: Input tokens written to the cache.

cache_read_tokens.$comment: Fits in 64 bits; the Rust reader enforces it.
cache_read_tokens.description: Input tokens served from the cache.

cost_usd.description: The cost in US dollars, a finite number, if the harness reports it.

input_tokens.$comment: Fits in 64 bits; the Rust reader enforces it.

output_tokens.$comment: Fits in 64 bits; the Rust reader enforces it.

scope.description: Whether the counts are one message's or the session's running total.

Finite.description: A finite real number: neither `NaN` nor infinite. Negative zero is finite.

Name.description: A plain name, such as that of a harness, a reader, a plug-in or a treatment: non-empty, with neither `@` nor white space.

NameVersion.$comment: The major, minor and patch numbers each fit in 64 bits; the parser enforces it.
NameVersion.description: An evaluator or instrument reference, `name@version`, split at the last `@`: the name is non-empty and holds neither `@` nor white space, and the version is `SemVer` 2.0.

RawFileRef.description: The streams the raw files of a trace archive, each with the digest of its file.

digest.description: The digest of the framed raw file of the stream.

stream.description: The name of the archived stream.

RawRef.description: A pointer to one frame: the stream and the index of the frame, counting the lines after the header from 0.

frame.$comment: Fits in 64 bits; the Rust reader enforces it.
frame.description: The index of the frame, from 0.

stream.description: The stream the frame belongs to.

ReasonCode.description: A reason code: a lowercase letter, then lowercase letters, digits or `_`.

SessionId.description: The id of a session: non-empty, with neither `#` nor white space, so that it reads as the session part of an `event:<session-id>#<seq>` evidence reference. A child session's id is its parent's id, `/`, and the id of the call that started it.

SessionSource.$comment: The major, minor and patch numbers each fit in 64 bits; the Rust reader enforces it.
SessionSource.description: The harness and the reader that produced a session, written as an object with the names and `SemVer` versions of both.

harness.description: The name of the harness that ran the session.

reader.description: The name of the reader that normalised the session.

SpanId.description: The id of a harness call, which pairs a call with its result and names the child session the call started: non-empty, with neither `#` nor white space.

StreamName.description: The name of an archived stream: `stdout`, `stderr`, or the name of a collected file, matching `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*`.

Timestamp.$comment: The pattern states the lexical form; a date or time that names no instant, such as month 13, and a fraction of more than nine digits are refused by the parser.
Timestamp.description: An RFC 3339 timestamp with an uppercase `T` and an explicit offset, `Z` or `±HH:MM`.

ToolOrigin.description: Where a tool call is served from: an object whose `kind` is `builtin`, `mcp`, with the `server` that offers the tool, or `other`.

oneOf.description: A tool the harness itself provides.
A tool an MCP server offers.

server.description: The name of the MCP server.

oneOf.description: Any other source.

UsageScope.description: What a usage event counts: one message, or the running total of the session, where a later `session_total` of a session supersedes an earlier one.

oneOf.description: The usage of one message, reported once, on the first line that carries the message id.
The running total of the session so far; a later one supersedes an earlier one.

WrappedCall.description: One MCP call that a bundling tool call contains: the tool it names and where the tool is served from.

name.description: The name of the wrapped tool.

origin.description: Where the wrapped tool is served from.

description: One line of a trace file: an object whose `kind` is `header`, `session` or `event`.

oneOf.description: The first line of the file.

raw.description: The raw files the trace was read from; every `raw_ref` of the file names one of their streams.

reader.description: The reader and its version, as `name@version` with a `SemVer` version.

oneOf.description: A session, after the header and before every event.

ended_at.description: When the session ended, if the harness or the frame times say.

id.description: The id of the session: non-empty, with neither `#` nor white space; a child's id is its parent's id, `/`, and the id of the call that started it.

model.description: The model the session ran, as the harness names it, if it says.

parent_session.$comment: The session id is this id followed by `/` and a non-empty call id; JSON Schema cannot state this, and the Rust reader enforces it.
parent_session.description: The id of the session that started this one; the session's own id is that id, `/`, and a call id.

raw_ref.description: The frame the session starts at.

source.description: The harness and the reader that produced the session.

started_at.description: When the session started, if the harness or the frame times say.

oneOf.description: An event with the session it belongs to.

session.description: The id of the session the event belongs to.
